title: Postpartum Hemorrhage
scenario: A 29-year-old client is 45 minutes post vaginal delivery of a 4.2 kg newborn after a prolonged, oxytocin-augmented labor. The nurse is called to the room because the perineal pad has become saturated and the client feels light-headed.

lines: G3P3 client 45 minutes post spontaneous vaginal delivery. Reports feeling light-headed and 'gushing.' Perineal pad saturated with bright red blood and passing clots. Fundus palpated above the umbilicus, boggy, and deviated to the right. Skin pale and diaphoretic. Alert and oriented x3.
Fundal massage initiated; large clots expressed. Bladder distended and palpable above symphysis. Client encouraged to void; unable. Second large-bore IV started. Labs drawn. Provider notified.
Straight catheterization performed for 650 mL clear urine. IV oxytocin infusion increased per order. Estimated cumulative blood loss now 900 mL. Continuous fundal assessment ongoing.
Fundus firm at umbilicus and midline. Lochia moderate, no further clots. Skin warm and color returning. Client reports light-headedness resolved.
Oxytocin 10 units in 500 mL lactated Ringer's, infusing
Perform fundal massage and express clots
Increase oxytocin infusion to 40 units in 500 mL LR
Straight catheterize if unable to void
Type and crossmatch 2 units packed red blood cells
Weigh perineal pads to quantify blood loss
Notify provider for continued heavy bleeding or SBP < 90

children.subject: Maternal-Newborn
children.rationale: A boggy displaced fundus, heavy bleeding with clots, tachycardia with hypotension, and pallor with diaphoresis all point to uterine atony and hypovolemia and require immediate action.

children.subject: Maternal-Newborn
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it supports uterine atony, hypovolemia, or both. Each finding may support more than one.

rows.text: Fundus deviated by a distended bladder

children.rationale: A boggy fundus and a bladder-displaced uterus reflect atony that prevents contraction, while tachycardia, hypotension, and a falling hemoglobin reflect volume loss.

children.subject: Maternal-Newborn
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1} caused by {2}.
children.rationale: The saturated pads, clots, and falling vitals identify excessive blood loss as the priority, and the boggy fundus identifies uterine atony as the most likely cause of early postpartum hemorrhage.

children.subject: Maternal-Newborn
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Place the client in reverse Trendelenburg
Restrict IV fluids to reduce bleeding

children.rationale: Fundal massage, emptying the bladder, and increasing oxytocin all promote uterine contraction. Reverse Trendelenburg and fluid restriction worsen hypovolemia and are contraindicated.

children.subject: Maternal-Newborn
children.stem: Which actions should the nurse take now? Select all that apply.

options.text: Weigh perineal pads to quantify blood loss
Ensure a second large-bore IV is patent
Vigorously massage the fundus continuously for one hour

children.rationale: Fundal massage until firm, quantifying blood loss, and maintaining IV access are appropriate. Continuous vigorous massage causes uterine fatigue, and holding oxytocin would worsen atony.

children.subject: Maternal-Newborn
children.stem: Which findings indicate the interventions have been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Fundus firm at the umbilicus and midline
Lochia moderate with no further clots

children.rationale: A firm midline fundus, controlled lochia, normalized vital signs, and improved perfusion show the hemorrhage is resolving. A persistently boggy fundus would signal continued atony.
